Easywurld — 30-day calendar: 11 posts and 2 stories a day

Monday 2 November–Tuesday 1 December 2026 · Africa/Lagos (WAT, UTC+1)

330 core posts · 60 stories · 26 LinkedIn posts · 1196 platform placements.

Strategy before production

Active campaign: Monday 2 November–Tuesday 1 December 2026 Platforms: TikTok, Instagram and Facebook, plus LinkedIn for siphoned posts Volume: 11 content posts + 2 stories per day on TikTok, Instagram and Facebook = 39 scheduled placements per day, plus 26 LinkedIn posts across the month. 1,196 placements in total. Timezone: Africa/Lagos (WAT, UTC+1)

This replaces the 22-post weekday plan. The owner wants a high-volume, series-led channel. The strategy below keeps that volume but makes it repeatable, recognisable and reviewable.

1. Is the idea good?

Yes — the series structure is the strongest part. It gives people recurring reasons to follow: niche ideas, myth-checking, trend analysis, AI workflows, humour, offer education, copywriting lessons and a daily introduction to Easywurld.

The risk is not the number 10. The risk is publishing 10 versions of the same generic tip, or 10 hard sells, every day. We avoid that by giving each slot a distinct job, rotating the offer, varying the format, and adapting the copy to each platform.

Rule: 10 core ideas per day, not 30 separate ideas. Each idea is produced once and adapted for TikTok, Instagram and Facebook. That is 30 placements, but one production system.

2. Positioning

Easywurld helps small businesses make the message, website, content and follow-up work together.

Audience: owner-led small businesses in Lagos and across Nigeria. Business objective: relevant WhatsApp enquiries, well-matched DIY pack sales, and scoped project briefs. Voice: plain, specific, useful, slightly witty. No fake client results, no inflated marketing promises.

The account should feel like a useful marketing studio thinking out loud: here is what we would post, here is what we would question, here is what we would automate, here is what we would steal from great copywriters, and here is who we are.

LinkedIn pulls

LinkedIn is not a fourth version of the same daily post. Six posts a week are siphoned from work that already exists: Monday a carousel write-up as a document post, Tuesday a teach post, Wednesday a show post, Thursday a trust post, Friday the week's best vertical video, Saturday an offer lesson. Thursday and Friday are the strongest reading days; Sunday stays quiet.

Story 11 — One Last Thought

The persona is defined in [AVATAR_OPERATOR.md](./AVATAR_OPERATOR.md).

A faceless, unhurried voice at 22:00. One flat sentence, one turn, one line worth repeating, one ask. The face is never shown; the night desk, the notebook and the voice carry the identity. It exists to make the account feel like a person with a point of view rather than a queue of posts, and to build a fixed evening habit. Everything about it is disclosed: AI presenter · Easywurld.

Series 1 — If I ran this account

Prompt: “If I was managing social media for a [niche] in Lagos, this is what I would post this week.”

Each episode gives three post ideas, one mistake to avoid and one first action. Rotate niches: fashion, food, beauty, fitness, property, education, events, logistics, retail, services. Do not pretend Easywurld manages these accounts. Say “if I ran” or “here is the plan I would test.”

Series 2 — Marketing Myth Court

Prompt: “Marketing myth: [claim]. Verdict: [true / false / it depends]. Here is the test.”

Do not debunk with another absolute. Use verdicts: mostly false, partly true, depends on the goal. Give a small test the owner can run. Examples: “post every day”, “hashtags are dead”, “you need a website before content”, “AI can replace strategy”, “more followers means more sales”.

Series 3 — Trend Desk

Prompt: “This week’s trend watch: [format]. Should a small business use it? Here is the Easywurld adaptation.”

Trend posts must be verified before recording. Use TikTok Creative Center, Instagram Reels feed, platform newsrooms and dated trend reports. Save the source URL, date checked and example link in the production sheet. Do not invent a trend or use an unlicensed song because it is trending.

For launch week, candidate formats reported in late October 2026 include Brand Vibe, Pick Your Emoji, Gold Star Behavior, interface-as-content and short proof Reels. These are candidates, not guaranteed current trends. Recheck on 1 November. 2 1 5

Series 4 — AI Automation Build

Prompt: “One AI workflow a small business can test: [workflow]. Input → AI draft → human check → next action.”

Show the boundary. AI can draft, classify, summarise or prepare. A human approves prices, promises, legal/health/finance answers and customer-sensitive replies. Use real screen recordings or clearly labelled concept demos. Do not imply a workflow is live if it is a sample.

Series 5 and 8 — Two memes

One owner-life meme and one marketing/AI/client meme per day. Scene-led, not a wall of text: a real photograph of the moment (the empty plastic chairs, the face-down phone, the blank screen), with a small two-line caption in the lower third. Eight scene plates are supplied in marketing/assets/meme-scenes/. No stolen meme templates with unclear rights, no fake customer screenshots, no punching down at customers. The caption under the post carries the useful lesson.

Series 6 and 9 — Two offer posts, one daily offer

Feature one offer per day. Post A explains the problem and contents. Post B handles an objection, limitation or next step. Rotate the nine packs. Do not sell nine packs in one day.

Current source price: ₦5,000 per DIY pack. Confirm price, contents, payment and delivery before publishing. State what the pack does not do. Custom projects are separate.

Series 7 — Steal This Copy Move

Prompt: “Steal this copy move from [expert]: [principle]. Don’t steal their words. Steal the structure. Here is an original Easywurld example.”

Break down the technique, not long copyrighted ads. Use short examples, attribute the source, and create a new Lagos/small-business example. Rotate Ogilvy, Schwartz, Sugarman, Halbert, Hopkins, Caples, Wiebe, Harry Dry and others. Marketing Examples and Copyhackers are useful modern reference points. 1 1

Series 10 — Meet Easywurld

A new introduction every day, not the same bio repeated. Rotate: who we serve, what we do, how we work, what we don’t do, sample tour, process, AI policy, handover, pricing philosophy, how to brief us, what happens after you message, why we label samples, and what we are building.

4. Format mix

The series are the structure; the format changes inside them.

  • AI talking head: myth verdicts, offer objections, and the 22:00 Operator close.
  • Screen demo: AI workflows, trend recaps, sample tours.
  • Carousel: niche plans, checklists, offer contents, copy breakdowns.
  • Scene-led static meme: the two daily meme slots.
  • Story frames: the two daily stories (poll/quiz and behind-the-desk).
  • Text post / document: the six weekly LinkedIn pulls.

Do not make every slot a talking head. The feed needs visual variety. The Operator is a production tool and a recognisable voice, not the entire brand.

5. Platform adaptation

PlatformAdaptation
TikTokNative vertical video, spoken hook, fast first frame, captions, one CTA. Static memes can be photo posts or short text videos.
InstagramReel or carousel depending on the idea. Carousel copy can be more structured. Check crop and safe areas.
FacebookNative text + image/video or carousel. Caption can be slightly more conversational. Do not just paste TikTok text with hashtags. Stories posted +5 minutes after Instagram.
LinkedInRewritten from the same idea, never pasted. First line is the whole hook, paragraphs of one or two lines, no hashtag block (two tags maximum), link in the first comment. One document post and one native video a week at most.

One core idea can have three captions. The hook and CTA stay consistent; the wording and format fit the platform.

6. AI talking-head rules

The AI presenter is the anonymous Operator persona — faceless founder, night desk, warm lamp, calm low voice. Full persona, delivery card, five scripts, script formula and 30-night arc: [AVATAR_OPERATOR.md](./AVATAR_OPERATOR.md). Scene plates and voice samples: marketing/assets/avatar/.

Because no face is shown, no real likeness or photo release is needed. That removes the last blocker on the talking-head slots. Never describe the Operator as the owner's real face, never use the fictional demo founder image, and disclose every clip as AI presenter · Easywurld.

TikTok requires disclosure for realistic AI-generated media, including a person portrayed saying something they did not say. Enable the platform AI setting and keep a visible label. 1

House style: chest-up, eye-level, natural light, restrained gestures, corrected phrase captions, one useful cutaway, no logo intro, no long end card. CapCut’s guidance supports meaningful jump cuts paired with reframes or cutaways rather than decorative transitions. 1

Use own/licensed audio or TikTok’s Commercial Music Library with the applicable rights. A trending personal-account sound is not automatically cleared for a brand. 1

7. Production system for 11 posts and 2 stories a day

Batch by series, not by day.

  • Sunday: write/verify the week’s 77 core ideas. Record Operator batches by series. Record screen demos. Design memes and carousels from templates. Render the week’s 14 stories and siphon the LinkedIn set.
  • Daily: assemble the 11 posts and 2 stories, adapt captions, QA, schedule.
  • Weekly: review series performance, not just individual posts.

Suggested batch blocks:

  1. Niche plans: 7 episodes.
  2. Myth Court: 7 Operator clips.
  3. Trend Desk: research + 7 recaps.
  4. AI Build: 7 workflows.
  5. Memes: 14 scene-led originals.
  6. Offer: one pack, 14 posts.
  7. Copy Move: 7 lessons.
  8. Meet Easywurld: 7 angles.
  9. One Last Thought: 7 Operator closes (batch with slot 2; same voice, same preset).
  10. Stories: 14 three-frame sequences.
  11. LinkedIn: 6 siphoned posts, written last from the finished copy.

This is heavy. Use templates, one locked Operator voice, caption presets and a shared asset library. If a slot fails QA, hold it rather than publishing unreviewed AI. The volume target stays 11 + 2; quality control is not optional.

8. Scheduling

TikTok’s official scheduler announcement describes a 15-minute to 10-day window and says scheduled posts must be deleted and re-uploaded to change them. Check current availability in your account. 1

Meta Business Suite can schedule Facebook and Instagram, but limits and features vary by account and surface. Check the planner in your own account. Do not assume a CSV auto-publishes.

The CSV in this repo is a production/planning sheet. Every row starts Draft. Mark Scheduled only after the platform confirms it. No social account is connected here.

9. Measurement

Review by series after 7 days:

  • Which series earns saves/shares?
  • Which earns watch time/completion?
  • Which earns profile visits and WhatsApp keyword enquiries?
  • Which offer gets qualified purchases or project briefs?
  • Which meme gets shares without attracting the wrong audience?

Keep 11 posts and 2 stories a day for the test, but change hooks, formats and angles based on evidence. Track the 22:00 Operator separately: if watch-through and follows climb during that slot, the persona is the asset, not the frequency. Do not declare a winner from one post. Do not invent month-end results.

10. Trust rules

  • All portfolio work is concept/sample. Label it.
  • No fake testimonials, rankings, client results or campaign metrics.
  • Hypothetical businesses/chats are labelled example.
  • DIY packs are not custom projects.
  • Trend posts need a dated source check.
  • Copywriting posts attribute the principle and use original examples.
  • AI presenters/voices are disclosed.
  • Private CVs, identity sources, customer messages and payment details stay out of public Git.

11. Launch gates

  • [ ] Confirm handles, website URL, WhatsApp and offer fulfilment.
  • [ ] Confirm the Operator persona and locked voice; no real likeness is required.
  • [ ] Render the week's story frames and confirm sticker placement in the preview.
  • [ ] Verify launch-week trends on 1 November.
  • [ ] Produce first 70 core posts / 210 platform adaptations.
  • [ ] QA captions, prices, disclosures, crops and audio rights.
  • [ ] Schedule only approved assets.
  • [ ] Record actual URLs and results afterwards.

2. Series rules

If I ran this account

  • Say “If I ran” or “I would test.” Do not imply Easywurld manages the business.
  • Give three post ideas, one mistake and one first action.
  • Use Lagos/Nigeria context where relevant, but do not invent local facts.
  • Label hypothetical businesses, prices and chats as examples.

Marketing Myth Court

  • Use a verdict: true, mostly false, partly true, false, or it depends.
  • Do not replace one absolute with another.
  • Give a small test the owner can run.
  • Do not claim platform rules without a current source.

Trend Desk

Trend posts are held until the verification log is complete.

  1. Check the dated source already attached to the brief.
  2. Within seven days before publishing, find a current public example on the target platform.
  3. Record the example URL, platform, date checked, rights check, relevance note and reviewer in marketing/TREND_VERIFICATION.csv.
  4. If the format is still relevant and rights are clear, update the script to say “this week” or “last week” only when the evidence supports it.
  5. If no current example is verified, publish only as a dated teardown: “Reported on [date]. Here is the structure.” Remove live-trend wording.

Late-October 2026 candidate formats include Brand Vibe, Pick Your Emoji, Gold Star Behavior, short proof Reels, native-interface tutorials and comment-keyword DM flows. These are candidates, not guaranteed November trends. 1 2 1

Do not use a trending personal-account sound for a brand unless the rights are cleared. TikTok Business Accounts should use the Commercial Music Library or separately licensed audio. 2

AI Automation Build

  • Show one workflow: input → AI draft → human check → output.
  • State what is not automated.
  • Use anonymised or fictional input.
  • Keep prices, promises, legal/medical/financial answers and complaints behind human review.
  • If using a repo demo, label it concept/sample. Do not imply it sent real messages or produced live results.

Memes

  • Two per day: one owner-life, one marketing/AI/client.
  • Original text-led graphics or short text videos.
  • Joke about the work, not the customer.
  • No fake notifications, stolen templates, private screenshots or punching down.
  • The caption carries the useful lesson.

Offer Spotlight A and B

  • One featured offer per day.
  • Post A: problem + actual contents + price + DIY boundary.
  • Post B: one objection or limitation + direct answer + same keyword CTA.
  • Rotate the nine packs. Do not sell all nine in one day.
  • Confirm price, contents, payment and delivery before publishing.
  • No guaranteed results, fake scarcity or invented testimonials.

Steal This Copy Move

  • Attribute the principle to the expert and source.
  • Steal the structure, not long copyrighted copy.
  • Use an original Easywurld/Lagos example.
  • Do not imply the expert endorses Easywurld.

Rotation: David Ogilvy, Eugene Schwartz, Joe Sugarman, Gary Halbert, Claude Hopkins, John Caples, Joanna Wiebe, Harry Dry, Ann Handley, Robert Bly.

Reference points: Ogilvy on research and headlines; Schwartz on existing desire and awareness; Sugarman on reading momentum; Halbert on market and offer; Hopkins on testing; Caples on self-interest headlines; Wiebe on voice-of-customer; Dry on concrete, checkable copy; Handley on utility and voice; Bly on benefits and clear CTAs. 1 1 2 1 1 1

Meet Easywurld

  • A new angle and format each day.
  • Rotate: studio map, one-sentence studio, process, sample labels, service menu, FAQ, AI policy, handover, pricing boundary, brief template, contact route, audience map, sample tour, series map, website anatomy, follow-up flow, local checklist, proposal anatomy, message worksheet, launch checklist, tool stack, behind the calendar, homepage tour, boundaries, who we serve, how to start, review rhythm, invitation, dictionary.
  • Do not invent team size, office, clients or results.
  • Do not use the fictional demo founder as the owner.

One Last Thought (22:00, the Operator)

  • One flat sentence, one turn, one line worth repeating, one ask. 18–24 seconds.
  • No greeting, no logo at the open, no shouting, no urgency. The face is never visible.
  • Same voice, same preset, same frame every night. The repetition is the brand.
  • Never invent a story about the owner. Lines about the work are safe; lines about a lived event need confirmation.
  • Full persona and scripts: [AVATAR_OPERATOR.md](./AVATAR_OPERATOR.md).

Story A — Poll / quiz (12:30)

  • Frame 1: the question. Frame 2: two options. Frame 3: the answer plus one sentence of reasoning.
  • One tap only. No link on a poll story. The point is a signal and a habit, not a sale.
  • Never write a question whose answer shames the audience.

Story B — Behind the desk (21:00)

  • Frame 1: the desk scene. Frame 2: tomorrow's 07:00 hook. Frame 3: link sticker to the site or the lead post.
  • It teases tomorrow's work; it never sells directly.
  • If tomorrow's post is a held Trend Desk, do not tease a live-trend claim.

LinkedIn pulls

  • Six a week, siphoned from work that already exists. Never paste a TikTok caption.
  • First line carries the whole hook. Paragraphs of one or two lines. Two tags maximum. Link in the first comment.
  • Monday's document post and Friday's video are the only heavy assets; the rest are text.
  • Thursday and Friday are the reading days; Sunday stays quiet.

Psychology layer

Every post in this calendar carries exactly one persuasion principle. Not as a trick — as a discipline. If the principle only works when we exaggerate, we drop the principle and keep the honest version.

Rule: one principle per post, named in the brief and in the CSV (Psychology move). The copy must still be useful if the reader never buys anything.

1. The twelve principles

KeyPrincipleWhat it doesWhere it appearsGuardrail
cognitive-easeCognitive ease — Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011)Easy-to-read ideas feel truer and saferShort sentences, one idea per slide, wide spacingNever use simplicity to hide a limitation
loss-aversionLoss aversion — Kahneman & Tversky, Prospect Theory (1979)People move faster to stop a loss than to chase a gain"This is what the unanswered message costs you"No fake countdowns or invented scarcity
curiosity-gapCuriosity gap — Loewenstein (1994)A specific open question pulls attention forwardMyth claims, copy breakdowns, Operator cold linesClose the loop in the same post
specificitySpecificity — Heath & Heath, Made to Stick (2007)Numbers, names and dates read as evidenceNiche plans, dated trend teardownsOnly numbers we can defend
social-proofHonest social proof — Cialdini, Influence (1984)Behaviour follows behaviourProcess posts, questions owners ask, labelled samplesNo invented clients, testimonials or results
reciprocityReciprocity — Cialdini (1984)Give the structure before askingFree checklists, workflows, slide copyThe post must be useful alone
authority-restraintAuthority through restraint — Cialdini (1984)Calm, sourced, unhurried statements read as authorityThe Operator slot, myth verdictsNo claimed credentials or awards
anchoringAnchoring — Tversky & Kahneman (1974)The first number sets the frameOffer carousels: contents → price → boundaryNo fake "was ₦X" pricing
peak-endPeak-end rule — Kahneman (1999)People remember the strongest and the last moment22:00 Operator close, meme punchlinesThe last line must be true and useful
mere-exposureMere exposure — Zajonc (1968)Familiar shapes become liked shapesMeet Easywurld repetition, fixed frames, fixed voiceRepeat the format, not the sentence
identityIdentity and in-group — Berger, Contagious (2013)People share what says something about themScene-led memesNever punch down at customers or staff
objection-reliefObjection relief — Cialdini (1984); Rackham, SPIN Selling (1988)Name the doubt before the buyer doesOffer Spotlight BAnswer honestly, including "no"

3. The five-line skeleton every post follows

  1. Interrupt — a flat, specific first line that stops the scroll (curiosity gap or loss aversion).
  2. Name the real problem — in the reader's words, not ours.
  3. Give the receipt — one checkable detail: a dated source, a pack contents list, a step order.
  4. State the limit — what this does not do (objection relief, authority through restraint).
  5. One ask — the smallest next step.

Posts that cannot fill line 3 do not get published. That rule kills most inflated content before it starts.

4. Applied examples

Myth Court — "posting every day guarantees growth"

  • Interrupt: "Posting every day guarantees growth. No."
  • Problem: frequency is being used to avoid making a decision.
  • Receipt: one week of series posts vs a previous week, measured on saves and enquiries.
  • Limit: this does not fix an unclear offer.
  • Ask: save the test.

Offer Spotlight A — PLAYBOOK ₦5,000

  • Interrupt: "The price is the easy part. The contents are the argument."
  • Problem: buyers cannot see what they are paying for.
  • Receipt: the four named deliverables, the exact price, the DIY boundary.
  • Limit: not custom work, no guaranteed results.
  • Ask: message the keyword.

Operator — 22:00

  • Interrupt: one flat, surprising sentence.
  • Turn: the real mechanism.
  • Close: a line worth repeating.
  • Silence on the last frame.

5. What is banned

  • Manufactured urgency, fake scarcity, "only 2 slots left".
  • Invented testimonials, revenue, follower counts or client names.
  • Borrowed lifestyle photos implying wealth we do not have.
  • Fear framing about customers or competitors.
  • Dark patterns in the CTA (pre-ticked boxes, fake chat screenshots).
  • Any principle used to make a false claim land harder.

6. Measurement tells us whether the psychology worked

After seven days, compare per series: saves (reciprocity, specificity), shares (identity), sticker taps (commitment), keyword enquiries (anchoring, objection relief), comment quality (curiosity gap). Change one lever a week. A principle is only validated by behaviour, not by how clever the line felt.

Sources are books and papers, cited by author and year. No framework here depends on a claim we cannot point to.

Hook / first frame

If I ran a fashion designer account in Lagos, this is what I would post this week.

Exact slide copy

Slide 1: If I ran a fashion designer account in Lagos, this is what I would post this week. Slide 2: Three posts I would test: 1. a fitting-room clip showing one garment on three body types 2. a fabric-care answer customers can save 3. a made-to-order timeline with honest milestones Slide 3: One mistake to avoid: posting only finished dresses. Slide 4: First action: Show the fitting decision, not just the final dress. Slide 5: This is a planning example, not a claim that Easywurld manages this account. Which idea would you test first?

EW-D01-S02 · Myth Court: Posting every day guarantees growth.

  • Pillar: Trust

Hook / first frame

Marketing myth: Posting every day guarantees growth.

Exact spoken script

Marketing myth: Posting every day guarantees growth Verdict: It depends. Frequency can create more chances to learn, but it does not fix an unclear offer or weak content. Ten useful series posts are different from ten random posts. Test it: Compare one week of consistent series posts with the previous week using saves, profile visits and relevant enquiries. That is Myth Court: keep the useful part, drop the absolute.

  • 0–3s: Operator, chest-up, myth on screen.
  • 3–12s: verdict: It depends..
  • 12–24s: the nuance, one labelled example.
  • 24–34s: the test: Compare one week of consistent series posts with the previous week using saves, profile visits and relevant enquiries.
  • 34–40s: one CTA.

Hook / first frame

Trend Desk: Brand Vibe — use the structure, not the hype.

Exact spoken script

Trend Desk: Brand Vibe. Drizzle Digital Vol. 40 reported it on 26 October 2026: a product front and center with four still shots that express the brand vibe. The business adaptation: Use one real product or service outcome with four owned images that show the customer's world. Do not invent a lifestyle. Before posting, verify a current example and the audio rights. This is a dated teardown, not a live trend claim. Save the filter, not the hype.
